title: In town
cando: ask where a place is and understand simple directions

about.text: This lesson is about places in town. You ask the way. You say the answer back to check.
goals: Ask the way: Excuse me. Where is the bank?
Understand left, right and straight on.
Say it back to check: Straight on, then left?
Write the way to your home.

chapters.title: Where is the bank?
chapters.text:
This lesson is about places in town.
First, Amina asks the way.
She says: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
A man says: Go straight on. Then go left.
He speaks fast. Amina says: Slowly, please.

chapters.title: Say it back
chapters.text:
Start with excuse me. Then ask: Where is the bank, please?
Listen for left, right and straight on.
Then say it back, to check. Straight on, then left?
Your voice goes up at the end.

chapters.title: Signs in town
chapters.text:
Next, you read signs in town.
A sign says open or closed. A sign says exit.
Arrows show the way.
Then write the way to your home.

chapters.title: Three places
chapters.text:
Then ask the way to three places.
Say each answer back. Left? Next to the bank?
Is it fast? Say: Slowly, please.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story. It is about a town.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again.

warmup.prompt: You are new in a town. What do you do?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people do all three. In this lesson, you ask someone.

conversation.title: Excuse me, where is the bank?
conversation.setting: Amina is new in town. She asks a man in the street.
lines: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
Go straight on. Then go left.
OK. Go straight on. Then left.
Yes. The bank is on the right.
On the right. Is it far?
No, it isn't. It's next to the market.
Next to the market? Thank you.
And where is the bus stop?
On the left. Thank you very much.

questions.q: Where does Amina want to go first?
questions.why: Amina asks: Where is the bank, please?

questions.q: What is the way to the bank?
questions.why: The man says: Go straight on. Then go left.
The man says: It's next to the market.

phrases.text: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
phrases.use: Asking the way. Start with excuse me.
Do not go left or right.
Asking: is it a long way?

items.meaning: Say it first. Then ask your question.
items.example: Excuse me. Where is the station?
I work in a small shop.

items.meaning: People sell food there, often outside.
items.example: I buy fruit at the market.

items.meaning: Trains and buses start and stop there.
You wait for the bus there.
items.example: The bus stop is on the right.

items.meaning: A road in a town. It has houses and shops.
The side where your heart is.
items.example: The bank is on the left.

items.meaning: Keep going. Do not go left or right.
items.example: Go straight on to the station.
Can you say it slowly, please?
Is it far? No, it isn't.

sound.title: Your voice goes up to check
sound.explain: Say it back to check. Your voice goes up at the end. Listen, then say each one.

sayIt.instructions: Say Amina's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Does your voice go up when you check?
lines: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
On the right. Is it far?
Next to the market? Thank you.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation.
examples: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
Go straight on. Then go left.
spot.question: Which one asks the way? Which one gives the way? Which one says it back, to check?
spot.answer: Excuse me + Where is the … + please asks the way. Go + straight on, left or right gives the way. Amina says it back with a question: Straight on, then left? Now she can check.

rules.title: Asking the way
rule: Ask: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
The way: Go left. Go right. Go straight on.
Where it is: It's on the left. It's on the right.
Say it back to check: Straight on, then left?
rules.mistake: Not: Where is bank? Say: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?

practice.q: ___ me. Where is the station, please?
practice.why: Excuse me: say it first, then ask.
Shops is more than one, so where are.

practice.q: Don't go left or right. Go ___ on.
practice.why: Straight on: do not go left or right.
Say on the right, or on the left.

practice.q: He says: Go left. You say it back: ___
practice.why: Say the same word back, to check.

practice.q: He speaks very fast. You say: ___ , please.
Is the station ___ ? No, it's near.

practice.why: Next to: at the side of the market.

practice.q: Excuse me. Where is the bus ___ ?
practice.why: A bus stop: you wait for the bus there.

yourTurn.prompt: You are new in a town. Write two questions to ask the way. Then write one answer back, to check.
starters: Excuse me. Where is the …, please?
yourTurn.model: Excuse me. Where is the station, please? Excuse me. Where is the market, please? Straight on, then right? Thank you.

text.title: Signs in town
text.body:
PRACTICE: signs in a made-up town

STATION
EXIT → Mill Road

MILL ROAD
← Bank
↑ Market, this way
→ Bus stop

BANK
Open 9 to 4
Closed on Sunday

MARKET
Open today, 8 to 2

KWAME'S SHOES
Sorry, we are closed today.

gist.q: Where can you see these signs?
gist.why: They are signs in the street: a road, a bank, a market.

gist.a: where places are, and when they are open
gist.why: The signs say the way to places, and the open times.

detail.q: You go out of the station. Where is Mill Road?
detail.why: EXIT → Mill Road: the arrow goes right.

detail.q: You are on Mill Road. Where is the bank?
It is Sunday. Can you go to the bank?
detail.why: The sign says: Closed on Sunday.

detail.q: When is the market open today?
detail.why: The sign says: Open today, 8 to 2.

items.meaning: It has short words. It tells you things.
items.example: Read the sign on the door.

items.meaning: Not open. You cannot go in.
items.example: The bank is closed on Sunday.

items.meaning: The door you use to go out.
Cars and buses go on it.
items.example: My flat is on Mill Road.

items.meaning: How you go to a place.
items.example: Is this the way to the station?

model.title: The way to my home
model.body:
From the bus stop:
Go straight on.
Go left at the market.
My street is Mill Road.
My flat is on the right.
It is next to the bank.

write.task: Write the way to your home, from a bus stop or a station. It can be real or made up. Copy the model. Then change the words.
checklist: I used left, right or straight on.
I wrote where my home is: on the left, on the right or next to …
Every sentence starts with a capital letter.

card.title: Three places
card.situation: You are new in town. You need the bank, the station and the market.
card.goal: Ask the way to all three. Say each answer back to check it.

phrases: Excuse me. Where is the station, please?
On the left? Next to the bank?
prepare.notes: Write the three places. Then write your questions: Excuse me. Where is the …, please?

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher gives the way to three places. Ask, then say each answer back. Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: You are a person in the street. I am new in town. I ask the way to the bank, the station and the market. Give me short directions: left, right, straight on. I say each one back. Tell me: yes or no. Use very short, simple sentences.

model.title: Three places
lines: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
Go straight on. It's on the left.
Go right. Then go straight on.
The market is next to the station.
Next to the station? Thank you very much.
compare: Did you start with excuse me?
Did you ask the way to three places?
Did you say each answer back, with your voice going up?

canDo: I can ask: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
I can understand left, right and straight on.
I can say an answer back to check it.
I can read signs in town: open, closed, exit.
I can write the way to my home.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. Where are the people? Where do they want to go?
reading.talk: What places are near your home? Write two or three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.q: You want to stop someone in the street. What do you say first?
quiz.why: Say excuse me first, then ask.

quiz.q: Do not go left or right. Go ___ .
quiz.why: Straight on: do not go left or right.

quiz.q: He says: It's on the right. You check: ___
quiz.why: Say the same words back, to check.

quiz.q: He speaks too fast. What do you say?
The bank is ___ on Sunday. You can't go in.
You want to go out of the station. Look for the ___ sign.
quiz.why: Exit: the door you use to go out.

quiz.q: I'm ___ . Can I have some water?
I am ___ a black coat today.
quiz.why: I am + wearing: this is now.
Two feet, so hurt, with no s.

liveClass: Day 1: stand up and point. Say left, right and straight on, and learners point. Then practise the conversation in pairs, with other places: the station, the market, the bus stop.
Day 2: the real-life task. Give the way to three places. Each learner asks, says each answer back, and asks for slowly, please, once.
Day 3: talk about the book. Then two learners read the way to their home aloud.
